MultiCash Payment Files

Domestic, urgent, direct-debit and foreign payments exported as MultiCash files (CFD, CFU, CFA, MT101), from an OCA payment order or an Enterprise batch payment.

Version19.0.2.2.0
EditionCommunity and Enterprise
LicenceAGPL-3
Requiresaccount_payment_order, account_cz_bankfile_base, base_iban

What it is for

MultiCash is the client application several Czech banks give their corporate customers for sending payment batches and fetching statements. It imports payment files in fixed formats. This module writes those files from an OCA payment order (account_payment_order), so it works on Community without any Enterprise module. On Enterprise, account_multicash_batch (delivered separately) writes the same files from a batch payment — see below.

The layouts follow Česká spořitelna's MultiCash 3.2 format description. The statement side of MultiCash (*.STA files in MT940) is imported by account_statement_import_mt940.

The formats

You choose the format by choosing the payment method. Each method writes one file type:

Payment method What it is File Currency and accounts
MultiCash CFD (Czech domestic transfer) domestic credit transfers .cfd CZK, Czech accounts only
MultiCash CFD (Czech direct debit / inkaso) domestic direct debits — you collect from your customers .cfd CZK, Czech accounts only
MultiCash CFU (Czech urgent transfer) urgent domestic transfers .cfu CZK, Czech accounts only
MultiCash CFA (foreign transfer) cross-border payments .cfa any currency; the beneficiary's account as entered (normally an IBAN)
MultiCash MT101 (SWIFT Request For Transfer) SWIFT MT101 transfer request .mt101 any currency; accounts as entered

"Czech account" means a CZ IBAN or [prefix-]number/bank code.

What goes into the file:

  • CFD / CFU: one block per payment with its own date, amount in hellers, both accounts, the names and addresses of payer and payee (from the company and the partner, up to four lines of 35 characters), VS, KS and SS, and up to four lines of message from the Communication. Text is upper-cased and encoded in code page 852.
  • CFA: a file header with the total and the count, then one SWIFT-like block per payment: payer, ordering account, beneficiary's account, name and address, the beneficiary's bank by BIC (or by name and address when the bank has no BIC), the payment details and the charge bearer. Code page 852.
  • MT101: one message for the whole file with a single execution date, then a transaction per payment. Plain ASCII.

Setting it up

  1. The bank journal (Accounting → Configuration → Accounting → Journals) needs its bank account. For CFD and CFU, and for the ordering account of CFA, it must be a Czech account. For CFA and MT101 the journal's bank must also have a BIC — the export refuses to run without one.
  2. A payment mode per format you use (Accounting → Configuration → Accounting → Payment Modes), with the matching MultiCash payment method and the journal. Use the direct debit / inkaso method on an inbound payment mode.
  3. Partners: a bank account on every partner you pay or collect from. For CFA and MT101 also the partner's address and country, and preferably the BIC of their bank.
  4. Recommended: l10n_cssk_payment_symbols, so the symbols of each bill reach the payment lines on their own (see account_abo for how).

Check with your bank which of the formats your contract covers — CFU, CFA and MT101 are often arranged separately.

Making a payment file

  1. Paying vendors: Accounting → Vendors → Payment Orders. Collecting by direct debit: Accounting → Customers → Debit Orders.
  2. New, choose the MultiCash payment mode, Create Payment Lines from Journal Items.
  3. Check Variable Symbol, Constant Symbol and Specific Symbol on the lines. An empty one is taken from a VS: / KS: / SS: token in the Communication; if there is none, the file carries 0. For a CFA payment set Priority (Urgent for express processing) and Charge Bearer (Shared, Payer, Beneficiary) on the line; they default to normal and shared.
  4. Confirm Payments, Generate Payment File. The file is attached to the order as <format>-<journal code>-<date and time>.<extension>.
  5. Import the file into MultiCash, send it to the bank from there, and mark the order with File Successfully Uploaded.

The order stops at the first problem it finds — a line without a bank account, a line with a zero or negative amount, a non-CZK line in CFD/CFU, an account that is not Czech where one is required, a missing BIC, and for MT101 lines dated differently.

Enterprise batch payments

account_multicash_batch (delivered separately) writes the same files from an Enterprise batch payment, with one payment method per format under the same names.

  • When it is installed, the bank journals of companies whose fiscal country is the Czech Republic get the two CFD methods (outgoing transfer, incoming direct debit); so do new bank journals of such companies. Journals of other countries do not get them, but can add them by hand. CFU, CFA and MT101 you add to the journal yourself (Outgoing Payments tab), once your bank has set them up for you.
  • Register the payments with the method of the format you want, group them in a batch (Accounting → Vendors → Batch Payments, or Customers for direct debits) and press Validate. The file is attached to the batch's chatter.
  • Before writing the file the batch lists every unusable payment: no recipient bank account, zero amount, for CFD/CFU a payment not in CZK or a recipient account that is not Czech, for CFA/MT101 a payment without a partner (the beneficiary's name and address would be empty).
  • MT101 has one execution date for the whole message, so every payment is executed on the batch date, with a warning for payments dated otherwise. CFD, CFU and CFA keep each payment's own date.
  • The urgency (priority) and the charge bearer of a CFA payment come from the payment's ISO 20022 fields when Odoo's ISO 20022 module is installed.

Both modules can be installed side by side.

Limitations

  • A credit note grouped with its invoice on the payment order (the payment mode's Group Transactions in Payment Orders) becomes one item of the net amount — the amount of the payment the order books. It carries the invoice's variable symbol; when one credit note is netted against several invoices their symbols differ and none is sent. Groups without a credit note keep one item per invoice. Without grouping, a credit-note line is refused.
  • Czech domestic formats. CFD and CFU take only CZK and Czech accounts; a Slovak IBAN is refused. CFA also needs the ordering account to be Czech.
  • MT101 from a payment order has one execution date for the whole message, so an order whose lines carry different dates is refused — set the order's Payment Execution Date Type to Fixed Date or Immediately, or split it.
  • Characters outside code page 852 (CFD, CFU, CFA) or ASCII (MT101) are reduced to their plain letters; MT101 also drops characters outside the SWIFT set.
  • The file is not uploaded to the bank automatically; MultiCash does that.
  • Only the Česká spořitelna layout was used as the specification. Other banks' MultiCash imports usually accept it, but test one file with your bank first.
